name: Complete Blood Count (CBC)
preparation: Fasting for 8-12 hours required. Avoid alcohol 24h before. Inform about any medications.
description: CBC measures red blood cells, white blood cells, hemoglobin, and platelets. Helps detect anemia, infections, and blood disorders.

name: Hemogram
description: Hemogram is a complete blood picture including RBC, WBC, platelet count, and differential leukocyte count.

name: Hemoglobin (Hb)
preparation: No fasting needed. Avoid heavy meals before test.
description: Measures hemoglobin levels in blood. Low levels indicate anemia, high levels may indicate polycythemia.

name: Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR)
description: ESR measures inflammation in the body. Elevated levels may indicate infection, autoimmune disease, or cancer.

name: Peripheral Smear (MP) - Malaria Parasite
description: Microscopic examination of blood to detect malaria parasites. Used when malaria is suspected.

name: Red Blood Cell Count (RBC)
description: Counts the number of red blood cells. Low count indicates anemia, high count may indicate polycythemia.

name: White Blood Cell Count (WBC)
description: Measures total white blood cells. High count indicates infection/inflammation, low count may indicate bone marrow issues.

name: Platelet Count
description: Counts platelets – essential for blood clotting. Low count increases bleeding risk.

name: Hematocrit (HCT)
description: Percentage of blood volume occupied by red blood cells. Helps diagnose anemia or polycythemia.

name: Mean Corpuscular Volume (MCV)
description: Average size of red blood cells. Helps classify anemia as microcytic, normocytic, or macrocytic.

name: Mean Corpuscular Hemoglobin (MCH)
description: Average amount of hemoglobin per red blood cell. Low MCH indicates hypochromic anemia.

name: Mean Corpuscular Hemoglobin Concentration (MCHC)
description: Average concentration of hemoglobin in red blood cells. Helps differentiate anemia types.

name: Red Cell Distribution Width (RDW)
description: Measures variation in red blood cell size. High RDW indicates mixed anemia or early iron deficiency.

name: Absolute Neutrophil Count (ANC)
description: Count of neutrophils, a type of white blood cell. Low ANC increases infection risk (neutropenia).

name: Absolute Eosinophil Count
description: Measures eosinophils – high counts indicate allergies, asthma, or parasitic infections.

name: Reticulocyte Count
description: Measures young red blood cells. Helps evaluate bone marrow response to anemia.

name: Coagulation Profile
preparation: Inform if on blood thinners. No fasting required.
description: Assesses blood clotting ability. Includes PT, aPTT, INR. Used before surgery or for bleeding disorders.

name: Prothrombin Time (PT)
preparation: No fasting needed. Inform about warfarin or other anticoagulants.
description: Measures time taken for blood to clot. Used to monitor warfarin therapy and liver disease.

name: Activated Partial Thromboplastin Time (aPTT)
description: Measures intrinsic clotting pathway. Used to monitor heparin therapy and detect hemophilia.

name: International Normalized Ratio (INR)
description: Standardized measure of PT. Used to monitor warfarin therapy. Target INR 2-3 for most conditions.

name: D-Dimer
description: Detects blood clot breakdown products. Elevated in DVT, pulmonary embolism, or DIC.

name: Fibrinogen Level
description: Measures fibrinogen, a protein needed for clot formation. Low levels cause bleeding disorders.

name: Iron Deficiency Profile
description: Includes serum iron, TIBC, ferritin, transferrin saturation. Diagnoses iron deficiency anemia.

name: Vitamin B12 & Folate
description: Measures B12 and folate levels. Deficiency causes megaloblastic anemia and neurological issues.

name: Ferritin
description: Measures iron storage protein. Low ferritin indicates iron deficiency; high ferritin may indicate inflammation.

name: Serum Iron
preparation: Fasting for 8 hours. Avoid iron supplements for 24h.
description: Measures iron in blood. Abnormal levels indicate iron deficiency or overload (hemochromatosis).

name: Total Iron Binding Capacity (TIBC)
description: Measures capacity of transferrin to bind iron. High TIBC with low iron suggests iron deficiency.

name: Transferrin Saturation
description: Percentage of transferrin that is saturated with iron. Low levels indicate iron deficiency.

name: Liver Function Test (LFT)
preparation: Fasting for 8-12 hours. Avoid alcohol for 24h.
description: Measures liver enzymes (ALT, AST, ALP), bilirubin, proteins. Screens for liver damage or disease.

name: SGPT/ALT
description: Alanine aminotransferase – enzyme released during liver cell injury. High levels indicate hepatitis or liver damage.

name: SGOT/AST
description: Aspartate aminotransferase – found in liver, heart, muscle. Elevated in liver disease or muscle injury.

name: Alkaline Phosphatase (ALP)
description: Enzyme in liver, bone, intestine. High levels suggest bile duct blockage or bone disorders.

name: Gamma-Glutamyl Transferase (GGT)
preparation: Fasting for 8 hours. Avoid alcohol for 24h.
description: Liver enzyme sensitive to alcohol use. Elevated in alcoholic liver disease and bile duct problems.

name: Total Bilirubin
description: Measures total bilirubin – high levels cause jaundice. Indicates liver or gallbladder issues.

name: Direct Bilirubin
description: Conjugated bilirubin. Elevated in obstructive jaundice (gallstones, tumors).

name: Indirect Bilirubin
description: Unconjugated bilirubin. High levels in hemolytic anemia or Gilbert's syndrome.

name: Total Protein
description: Measures total protein (albumin + globulin). Abnormal levels indicate liver, kidney, or nutritional disorders.

name: Serum Albumin
description: Main protein in blood. Low levels indicate liver disease, kidney disease, or malnutrition.

name: Serum Globulin
description: Calculated from total protein minus albumin. High globulin seen in chronic infections or multiple myeloma.

name: Albumin/Globulin Ratio
description: Ratio of albumin to globulin. Low ratio suggests liver disease or autoimmune conditions.

name: Renal Function Test (RFT)
preparation: Fasting for 8 hours. Avoid heavy protein meal.
description: Includes urea, creatinine, uric acid. Evaluates kidney function and detects kidney disease.

name: Blood Urea Nitrogen (BUN)
description: Measures urea nitrogen – waste product from protein breakdown. High levels indicate kidney dysfunction.

name: Serum Creatinine
description: Waste product from muscle metabolism. Elevated creatinine indicates reduced kidney function.

name: Uric Acid
preparation: Fasting for 8 hours. Avoid purine-rich foods (red meat, seafood).
description: End product of purine metabolism. High levels cause gout and kidney stones.

name: Lipid Profile
preparation: Fasting for 10-12 hours. Only water allowed.
description: Measures total cholesterol, HDL, LDL, triglycerides. Assesses cardiovascular risk.

name: Total Cholesterol
description: Total amount of cholesterol in blood. High levels increase heart disease risk.

name: HDL Cholesterol
description: Good cholesterol – helps remove excess cholesterol. Low HDL increases heart disease risk.

name: LDL Cholesterol
description: Bad cholesterol – deposits in arteries. High LDL is a major risk factor for heart disease.

name: Triglycerides
description: Type of fat in blood. High triglycerides increase risk of heart disease and pancreatitis.

name: Electrolytes Panel
description: Measures sodium, potassium, chloride. Detects imbalances due to dehydration, kidney disease, or medications.

name: Serum Sodium (Na+)
description: Maintains fluid balance. Low sodium (hyponatremia) or high sodium (hypernatremia) cause neurological symptoms.

name: Serum Potassium (K+)
description: Essential for nerve and muscle function. Abnormal levels cause arrhythmias or weakness.

name: Blood Glucose (Fasting)
description: Measures blood sugar after fasting. Used to diagnose diabetes and prediabetes.

name: Postprandial Blood Sugar (PPBS)
description: Blood sugar after eating. Helps assess glucose control in diabetics.

name: Random Blood Sugar (RBS)
description: Blood sugar at any time. Random level >200 mg/dL suggests diabetes.

name: Glycated Hemoglobin (HbA1c)
description: Average blood sugar over 3 months. Used to monitor diabetes control.

name: Insulin (Fasting)
description: Measures insulin levels. Helps diagnose insulin resistance and type 2 diabetes.

name: C-Peptide
description: Reflects insulin production. Differentiates type 1 from type 2 diabetes.

name: HOMA-IR (Insulin Resistance)
description: Calculated from fasting glucose and insulin. High score indicates insulin resistance, prediabetes.

name: C-Reactive Protein (CRP)
description: Marker of inflammation. High CRP indicates infection, arthritis, or heart disease risk.

name: High Sensitivity CRP (hs-CRP)
description: More sensitive CRP used to predict cardiovascular disease risk.

name: Dengue NS1 Antigen
description: Detects dengue virus early (first 5 days of fever). Positive indicates acute dengue.

name: Dengue IgG/IgM Antibodies
description: Detects antibodies after day 5. IgM indicates recent infection, IgG past infection.

name: COVID-19 Antigen
description: Rapid test for active COVID-19 infection. Positive within first 7 days of symptoms.

name: COVID-19 Antibody (IgG/IgM)
description: Detects past COVID-19 infection or vaccine response. IgG indicates immunity.

name: HIV 1&2 Antibody (Rapid)
description: Screening test for HIV. Positive results need confirmation by Western Blot.

name: HBsAg (Hepatitis B Surface Antigen)
description: Detects active Hepatitis B infection. Positive indicates contagious state.

name: Anti-HBs (Hepatitis B Antibody)
description: Detects immunity to Hepatitis B (after vaccination or recovery).

name: Anti-HCV (Hepatitis C Antibody)
description: Screening test for Hepatitis C. Positive requires RNA test to confirm active infection.

name: Widal Test (Typhoid)
description: Detects antibodies against Salmonella typhi. Used to diagnose typhoid fever.

name: Malaria Antigen (Pf/Pv)
description: Rapid test for malaria parasites (Plasmodium falciparum and vivax).

name: Chikungunya IgM/IgG
description: Detects chikungunya virus antibodies. IgM indicates recent infection.

name: Rheumatoid Factor (RF)
description: Autoantibody found in rheumatoid arthritis and other autoimmune diseases.

name: Thyroid Profile (Total T3, T4, TSH)
preparation: Fasting for 8 hours. Avoid biotin supplements.
description: Evaluates thyroid function. Diagnoses hyperthyroidism or hypothyroidism.

name: Free T3 (FT3)
description: Active form of T3. High in hyperthyroidism, low in hypothyroidism.

name: Free T4 (FT4)
description: Active thyroid hormone. Helps diagnose thyroid disorders.

name: Anti-TPO (Thyroid Peroxidase Antibody)
description: Autoantibody in Hashimoto's thyroiditis and Graves' disease.

name: Cortisol (Morning)
preparation: Fasting for 8 hours. Test between 8-9 AM.
description: Stress hormone. High levels suggest Cushing's syndrome, low levels Addison's disease.

name: Prolactin
preparation: Fasting for 8 hours. Avoid stress and breast stimulation.
description: Hormone that stimulates milk production. High levels cause infertility or galactorrhea.

name: Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH)
description: Regulates menstrual cycle and sperm production. High FSH suggests menopause or testicular failure.

name: Luteinizing Hormone (LH)
description: Triggers ovulation and testosterone production. Used in infertility evaluation.

name: Testosterone (Total)
preparation: Fasting for 8 hours. Test in morning.
description: Male sex hormone. Low levels cause low libido, fatigue; high levels may indicate tumors.

name: Vitamin D (25-Hydroxy)
description: Measures vitamin D status. Deficiency causes bone pain, muscle weakness, and osteoporosis.

name: Vitamin B12
description: Essential for nerve function and RBC production. Deficiency causes anemia and neuropathy.

name: Folate (Serum)
description: B vitamin needed for DNA synthesis. Deficiency causes megaloblastic anemia.

name: Autoantibody Panel (ANA)
description: Screening test for autoimmune diseases like lupus, scleroderma, and Sjogren's.

name: Urine Routine & Microscopy
preparation: Collect first morning urine midstream in sterile container.
description: Detects urinary tract infections, kidney disease, and diabetes via physical, chemical, and microscopic exam.

name: Urine Culture & Sensitivity
preparation: Collect clean catch midstream urine in sterile container.
description: Identifies bacteria causing UTI and determines effective antibiotics.

name: Stool Routine & Occult Blood
preparation: Avoid red meat, vitamin C, and NSAIDs for 3 days before.
description: Detects parasites, blood, and inflammation in stool. Used for gastrointestinal disorders.

name: Semen Analysis
preparation: Abstain from ejaculation for 2-5 days. Collect sample in sterile cup.
description: Evaluates male fertility – counts sperm, motility, morphology, and volume.

name: GeneXpert MTB/RIF
description: Molecular test for tuberculosis and rifampicin resistance. Fast and accurate.

name: PSA (Prostate Specific Antigen) - Total & Free
preparation: Avoid ejaculation for 48h. No DRE before test.
description: Screens for prostate cancer. Elevated PSA may indicate cancer or benign enlargement.

name: CA 125 (Ovarian Cancer Marker)
description: Tumor marker for ovarian cancer. Also elevated in endometriosis and pelvic inflammatory disease.

name: CEA (Carcinoembryonic Antigen)
description: Tumor marker for colorectal, lung, and breast cancers. Used to monitor treatment response.

name: AFP (Alpha-fetoprotein)
description: Tumor marker for liver cancer and germ cell tumors. Also used in prenatal screening.

name: Beta-hCG (Quantitative)
description: Measures pregnancy hormone. Used to confirm pregnancy, detect ectopic pregnancy, or monitor miscarriage.

name: NIPT (Non-invasive Prenatal Testing)
description: Screens for chromosomal abnormalities (Down syndrome, Edwards syndrome) using fetal DNA from mother's blood.
